candidates.title: Canonical answers with a bounded cutover
candidates.proposal:
Upgrade the prior “One canonical answer per policy question” route. Keep one substantive answer per question, descriptive links from other pages, visible named sources and review dates, and a small register tracking overdue answers, contradictions and reader failures. Change the cutover procedure: before treating a question as consolidated, the editor must inspect its known duplicate locations and search the static files for its distinctive old wording. Correct contradictory copies or replace them with links during that session. Unresolved contradictions remain open work; selecting a canonical URL alone does not close them.

This closes a consequential gap in the original route: a correct canonical answer can coexist with misleading copies while consolidation proceeds gradually. The editor owns both the answer and its cutover. Record the affected locations and completed edits before uploading, so an interruption leaves a usable restart point. Inspect the published locations afterward. If an old page cannot be edited, record it explicitly and avoid claiming that the question has been fully consolidated.

Start with a question whose affected files can plausibly fit one session. Use 20 minutes for new memos and reader reports, 70 for source verification, answer changes and duplicate removal, and 30 for publication checks and overdue entries. Every published substantive answer requires a named source and review date. An unsupported answer becomes a verification-pending notice. Existing answers missing that metadata enter the correction queue immediately.

Resources are the existing files, memo archive and a plain text register. An existing monitored inbox can collect failed searches; otherwise use brief observed reader checks. Compared with the original route, this spends more time completing each question before expanding coverage, but reduces the period when contradictory copies remain available. Search cannot establish complete coverage, and the editor must be able to change the relevant pages.
candidates.experiment: Within one two-hour session, the editor pilots one question with known duplicates. Use a historical revision or local copy if no suitable live change exists. Record editing time, conflicting passages left public, overdue or unsupported answers, and any failed attempts to reach current guidance. Interrupt preparation once and inspect whether the recorded locations let the editor resume without overlooking a copy. Ask two unfamiliar readers to start from different old locations and locate the current answer, source and review date. Stop expanding consolidation if this small cutover exceeds the weekly budget; retain the verified answer and completed links, keep unresolved locations open, and choose a smaller question next. Compare the extra cutover effort with the original route’s practice of carrying duplication as backlog; no benefit is assumed until inspected.

candidates.title: Dependency tracking with an explicit source-conflict rule
candidates.proposal:
Upgrade the prior “Trace policy changes to affected answers” route. Preserve its memo-to-passage register, searches for unregistered wording, visible source and review dates, overdue queue, contradiction tracking and reader-failure log. Change what happens when a newly discovered memo appears to revise an answer: before propagating its wording, the editor checks whether the archive establishes its scope, effective date and relationship to the answer’s existing source. A newer document date alone does not establish that it governs.

The editor records either a supported replacement relationship or a precise unresolved conflict. When applicability is established, update all linked passages and search for missed copies. When the sources genuinely conflict and the archive cannot resolve which governs, replace only the affected substantive guidance with a dated verification-pending notice naming the conflicting sources. Do not extend that withdrawal to unrelated answers. If the archive establishes that a revision takes effect later, retain the currently applicable guidance and record the future change for the appropriate weekly session.

This closes a prerequisite gap: the original change-propagation mechanism can efficiently spread the wrong interpretation when archive documents overlap. The editor owns the decision and retains the last verified text locally. If interrupted, unresolved rows remain open; they cannot be marked current merely because text was edited. Restore withdrawn guidance only after the archive supports its applicability, with a fresh review date. This workflow cannot settle policy ambiguities that the archive itself leaves unresolved.

Use a spreadsheet or plain text register and existing files. Within two hours, allocate 25 minutes to archive additions and source relationships, 65 to affected answers and conflicting pages, and 30 to overdue entries, missed-passage searches and reader reports. Collect search failures through an existing monitored address or brief observed checks. Compared with ordinary dependency tracking, the extra source check may delay publication and temporarily reduce available guidance, but limits unsupported policy changes. Pilot a small section because initial mapping and ambiguous sources may consume the budget.
candidates.experiment: The editor uses one two-hour session to inspect three archived cases where available: an explicit replacement, a later memo with different scope, and an ambiguous overlap. If the archive lacks a case, label a local hypothetical exercise clearly. Check whether each decision is supported by source wording and whether the resulting action updates, retains or withdraws only the appropriate passages. Search the files independently for missed affected wording. Record time, stale answers, unresolved contradictions, pending notices and reader failures, including whether a reader can identify the current answer and its review date. Stop expanding the register if source resolution repeatedly consumes the session or affected passages remain unmanageable. Keep verified mappings, narrow the next batch, and leave ambiguous claims withdrawn rather than treating completion of the register as resolution of policy.
